To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Epac protein inhibitor has no effect on vasoconstriction induced by serotonin, noradrenalin or KCl depolariation, but changes the contraction kinetics.
ESI 9, a selective inhibitor of Epac1 protein, has no effect on contractile responses to serotonin, noradrenalin and KCl depolarization in rat aorta.

the selective inhibitor Epacs protein ESI 09 eliminated the tonic phase of the aortic ring contraction induced by endogenous vasoconstrictive agents, which was associated with the suppression of the induced increase in the cytoplasmic concentration of Ca2+ by the Epac1 protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of Epac1 and its inhibitor ESI 9 in aorta of rats.
the role of Epac1 protein in the formation of vascular contractility in rats.
the possibility of using Epac1 protein inhibitors in the treatment of cardiovascular diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Epac protein inhibitor has an inhibitory effect on the tonic phase of vascular contractility in rats.
the cAMP independent activation of Epac1 protein is involved in the development of aortic contraction in response to vasoconstricting compounds.
ESI 009 has a significant effect on the contractile response of aorta to the influence of endogenic vasoactive substances and this effect is associated with the inhibition of the Epac1 protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Epac1 is involved in the formation of a tonic phase of contraction of rat aorta in response to the action of vasoconstricter compounds.

Epac1 and/or Epac2 proteins play a key role in the regulation of the contractility of aortic smooth muscle, and the Epac1 protein is involved in the development of the prolonged tonic contraction of vascular smooth muscle induced by endogenic agonists.

the Epac protein inhibitor eliminates the phase of prolonged contraction of the aorta caused by vasoconstrictive compounds, which is accompanied by the suppression of the induced growth in cytoplasmic calcium concentration in the aortic muscle cells of rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the selective Epac1 and/or Epac2 inhibitor ESI 05/09 can be used in the treatment of cardiovascular diseases associated with the formation of prolonged tonic contractions of smooth muscle cells.

ESI 009, an inhibitor of Epac1 protein, has a pronounced effect on vascular contractile activity, which is associated with a decrease in the duration of the tonic phase of contraction and a decrease in the amplitude of the contraction of aortic smooth muscle induced by serotonin, noradrenalin and KCl.
the Epac protein inhibitor has the ability to selectively eliminate the tonic phase of the contractile reaction in aortic rings caused both by the endogenic and exogenic vasoconstric-tive compounds.
